summary: The note describes Freikorps, right-wing paramilitary militias raised after World War I and during the German Revolution of 1918-19, largely from war veterans. They were nominally formed to support the government against Soviet-backed German Communists seeking to overthrow the Weimar Republic, but they also despised the Republic and carried out assassinations of its supporters. The Freikorps are described as a precursor to Nazism, with many volunteers later joining the SA.
one_line: Right-wing paramilitary militias of World War I veterans, raised in 1918-19 Germany, later seen as a precursor to Nazism.
key_facts: Freikorps were raised in the aftermath of World War I and during the German Revolution of 1918-19.
Freikorps consisted largely of World War I veterans.
Freikorps were ostensibly raised to fight on behalf of the government against Soviet-backed German Communists.
The German Communists were attempting to overthrow the Weimar Republic.
The Freikorps also despised the Weimar Republic.
Freikorps were involved in assassinations of supporters of the Republic.
The Freikorps were widely seen as a precursor to Nazism.
Many Freikorps volunteers ended up joining the Nazi militia, the Sturmabteilung (SA).
An entire series of Freikorps awards also existed.
